title: Maximum speed value
description: Essential: The final answer must be 1000 m/s.

title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Important: The solution must apply the work-energy theorem, stating that the kinetic energy gained equals the work done by the electric field (qU).

title: Charge-to-mass ratio derivation
description: Important: The solution must derive or use the ratio q/m from the given acceleration, Coulomb's law, and Newton's second law.

title: Correct potential difference
description: Important: The solution must correctly identify the electric potential difference U as 3000 V (potential at P minus potential at infinity).

title: Algebraic combination of expressions
description: Important: The solution must correctly combine the expressions for v, q/m, and U to eliminate q and m.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The final answer should have correct units (m/s) and intermediate calculations should maintain dimensional consistency.

title: Sign error in work or potential
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the work done by the electric force is given a positive sign or if the potential difference U is calculated incorrectly (e.g., infinity minus P).

title: Misinterpreting given acceleration
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the instantaneous acceleration at P is used directly in the energy equation without deriving the charge-to-mass ratio.
